Disrumpo.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A preset loaded from the browser kept the previous preset's shape settings** — Loading from the preset browser did not run the same code as a project reload. Each node remembers its shape settings for every distortion type, and the sound engine kept the previous preset's settings for every type except the one in use, so changing a node's type afterwards (by hand or by automation) played stale settings, and the next project save stored them. A browser load now takes the same path as a project reload, and the browser's Save stores exactly what the sound engine holds.
- **The Chaos distortion repeated a short cycle instead of evolving** *(shared DSP)* — In the Lorenz model at 44.1 and 48 kHz, the attractor was stepped too coarsely, briefly overshot its safety bound and was restarted about 36 times a second, so the distortion repeated the same 28 ms pattern. The attractor is now stepped finely enough at every sample rate and speed, and only a truly runaway state is restarted.
- **The Stepped modulation curve overshot its amount by a third** *(shared DSP)* — With the source at full scale (a macro at 100 %, a square LFO), a route or macro with the Stepped curve gave 4/3 of its amount. Its top step is now exactly the amount, so such routes move less than before at full scale.
- **Changing a modulation route's source or destination could jump** *(shared DSP)* — When a route switched source, destination or curve, it briefly applied the old route's amount to the new destination, which could cause a short burst or jump. A changed route now starts from its own amount.
- **Small load fixes** — A new instance ran the Rungler at 200 Hz, outside its range, until its Rate knob was moved; it now starts at the 4.09 Hz the knob shows. A project could restore Folds and Bit Depth between the steps their knobs offer; they now load on a step, as a browser load does.

Gradus.notes_markdown:
### Changed

- **Swing now plays long step first, and keeps swinging with the host playing** *(shared arp engine)* — Free-running, each swung pair played its short step first while the gates and ratchets were sized for the long one. With the host transport running, Gradus re-locked to the host every block, which undid the swing and could fire two notes a few milliseconds apart. Each step now lasts its own swung length, the long step comes first in both cases, and gates and ratchets fit the step they belong to. Every swung preset and project swings the other way round from before.

### Fixed

- **A gate above 100 % on a single held key played staccato** *(shared arp engine)* — When the same pitch was struck again while its previous note was still held, that older note's note-off cut the new note at the old gate length, so a legato gate (101-200 %) turned into 50 % notes. A re-struck pitch now ends the old note first and the new note keeps its full gate.
- **The first note after a pause could come late** *(shared arp engine)* — After all keys were released, the step counter stopped where it was, so the first note of the next phrase waited out the rest of that old step: up to 2 seconds at slow free rates. The first step now fires in the block the key is pressed.
- **The arp drifted off tempo when not following the host** *(shared arp engine)* — Step lengths derived from the tempo were cut down to a whole sample instead of rounded, so with the transport stopped or a free-running arp each step could be one sample short and the pattern drifted against the tempo. Step lengths now round to the nearest sample and swung pairs add up exactly.
- **Editing a Modifier lane step saved the wrong value** *(shared UI)* — A step clicked, pasted or transformed in the Modifier lane was saved as 17 times its flag value (the lane and the parameter used different scales). The sound was the same, but the saved value differed from the factory presets. The lane now saves the flags themselves.
- **Speed-curve depth was 0 after reopening a project** — After a project reload the arpeggiator played every lane's speed curve at depth 0 until a speed-curve control was touched. The saved depths now apply as soon as the project loads.
- **The Ratchet and Condition lanes swapped their speed-curve depths** — Each lane's depth knob drove the other lane. Each now drives its own. In older projects a curve drawn on the Ratchet tab may now show on the Condition tab, the lane it always played on.
- **A preset loaded from the browser and one restored by the host could play differently** — Loading from the preset browser did not run the same code as a host restore, so ratchet shuffle, lane speeds and a few clamped values could differ between the two. Both now load identically. The factory presets now store the ratchet shuffle they play (50, 66.67 or 75 %).
- **Resetting a lane speed to its default set it to 0.25x** — The eight lane-speed controls reported 0.25x to the host as their default, so a host "reset to default" (or double-click reset) slowed the lane to a quarter. Their default is now 1x, the speed a new instance starts at.

Innexus.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A preset loaded from the preset browser now loads all of it** — The preset browser read presets with a second, incomplete reader that never reached the sound engine directly: the envelope (ADSR) settings, voice mode, modulator tempo sync, the physical-model, impact, waveguide, bow, body and sympathetic settings, the stored memory slots and their envelopes were left as they were. A browser load now takes the same path as a project reload, so the whole preset is restored, including its stored sample, which is loaded again from its saved location.
- **The modulator Sync switches and note values showed the wrong setting after a project reload** — Reopening a project restored Mod 1 and Mod 2 Sync and Note Value in the sound, but the controls showed their defaults. They now show the restored values.

Iterum.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **Spectral mode's Feedback did almost nothing after the first repeat** *(shared DSP)* — The feedback limiter worked on unscaled FFT values, so it squashed every recirculated frequency down to the same tiny level: the repeats after the first fell away by tens of dB and lost their tone colour. The limiter now works in the signal's own scale, so Feedback sustains the repeats as set and keeps their spectrum. Patches with Spectral feedback above 0 repeat noticeably longer than before.
- **Spectral mode stepped at every analysis frame** *(shared DSP)* — The Spectral delay overlapped its frames without a synthesis window, so with feedback its output jumped at every frame edge (about every 10.7 ms at the default FFT size). It now uses matched analysis and synthesis windows, and the steps are gone.
- **The Digital, Tape and Spectral delays sounded different at different buffer sizes** *(shared DSP)* — The Digital delay applied its delay time and modulation once per audio block, so the modulation moved in steps and a bounce differed from real-time playback and between hosts. The Tape delay did the same for its heads and its hiss, and the Spectral delay's echo timing moved with the block size. All three now run sample by sample (the Spectral delay at a fixed latency), so the output is the same at every buffer size.
- **The Tape delay hissed with Wear and Age at 0** *(shared DSP)* — With Wear and Age both at 0 the Tape delay still added hiss at about -88 dBFS with no input, so Iterum never went silent in Tape mode. At Wear 0 and Age 0 it is now silent; any Wear or Age above 0 hisses as before.
- **Spectral mode's stereo spread changed from one render to the next** *(shared DSP)* — The random phase offsets behind the stereo spread were seeded from the plugin's memory address, so two instances, or the same project rendered twice, came out slightly different. They now start from a fixed seed and restart from it on every reset, so renders repeat exactly.

Membrum.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **A kit loaded from the browser did not fully replace the previous kit** — Loading a kit from the kit browser ran a separate copy of the kit loader in the editor instead of the one a project reload uses. It skipped the voice and coupling flush, so drums still ringing from the previous kit could carry over as a tonal beep or a ring that did not stop. It also left each pad's noise-layer level and the "default" body damping as they were, and did not update the macros. A browser load now runs the same code as a project reload.
- **A pad preset changed the pad's on/off state and pan, and skipped its noise layer** — Loading a pad preset onto a pad overwrote the pad's enabled state and pan, which a pad preset is meant to leave alone, and did not apply the preset's noise-layer level. Pad presets now load through the sound engine's own pad-preset code: enabled and pan are kept and the noise layer is applied.

Profundum.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **Sample & Hold and Smooth Random morph cycles repeated too soon** — The random generator behind these two cycle shapes overflowed and cycled after about 79,000 values instead of running its full sequence. It now runs the full sequence, so these shapes play a different random pattern than before.
- **The stereo field's band split lost precision at low frequencies** — Its crossover filters now run in double precision, which removes a small level error at low split frequencies, largest at high sample rates.
- **A possible crash when a host shut Profundum down with its window still open** — If a host shut down the plugin's controller before closing the editor window, the update banner kept checking for updates, twice a second, through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The update check now stays alive until the window is gone.
- **A possible crash when opening the preset browser after a host shut Profundum down with its window still open** — In the same situation, clicking Presets read the preset list through memory that had already been freed, which could crash the host. The preset list now stays alive until the window is gone.

- **Long preset descriptions were cut off in the preset browser** — The description under the preset list was a single line, so a long one ended mid-word at the edge. It now wraps onto up to three lines, ending with "…" if it is longer still, and hovering over it shows the whole text.

### Changed

- **Built with VST3 SDK 3.8.1.**

Ruinae.notes_markdown:
The first stable release. A full audit of Ruinae and the shared DSP it uses found about 215 problems; every one is fixed, or measured and documented, and regression tests now guard voices, oscillators, filters, effects, the arpeggiator, the mod matrix, presets and saved state.

### Added

- **Velocity > Amp** — A new knob (VEL, in the AMP envelope) sets how far note velocity scales the level. See "Note velocity never changed the level" below.
- **Voice LFO Rate and Shape** — The voice LFO had no rate or shape control. It now has both, defaulting to 1 Hz sine, so the presets that use it sound as before.

### Changed

- **Swing plays the long step first, also with the host playing** — Free-running swing played each pair short step first while gates and ratchets were sized for the long one, and with the host transport running Ruinae re-locked to the host every block, which undid the swing. Each step now lasts its own swung length, long first, and gates and ratchets fit their step. Swung presets and projects swing the other way round.
- **A free-rate arpeggio keeps running with the transport stopped** — Tempo-synced rates still follow the transport.
- **Voice routes to Filter Resonance use the global route's 10 Q scale** — Projects saved before this version keep their sound.

### Removed

- **The Gain Compensation switch** — It did nothing. Its parameter stays hidden, so saved projects still load.

### Fixed

- **A possible crash after switching editor tabs** — Switching the modulation source, the distortion view or the effects tab left the editor holding controls that no longer existed; editing afterwards could crash the host.
- **A damaged preset could hang the audio thread** — An extreme oscillator Phase Mod value in a preset or project took the audio thread into a near-endless loop. Every oscillator value now loads within its range.
- **Stuck notes from the arpeggiator and voice-mode changes** — Turning the arpeggiator off, changing its mode or resetting it with keys held, a slide step on a chord, and switching between Poly and Mono could leave notes sounding. Each path now ends every note it started, and arp resets send note-offs for notes already sent to the MIDI output.
- **Delay and reverb went silent after an engine reset** — After the host restarted processing (a sample-rate change, a bypass, a transport reset), the delay and the reverb stayed silent until their switches were toggled.
- **Switching between Plate and Hall glitched** — The reverb crossfade restarted every block and could fade an instance into itself. It now runs once and reverses cleanly when switched back mid-fade.
- **Pitch bend and tuning** — Mono mode ignored pitch bend and the tuning reference; pitch-bend smoothing depended on the buffer size; pitch bend, channel aftertouch and the mod wheel did not arrive through the host's MIDI mapping; mono Portamento Time was overwritten by the arpeggiator's Slide Time.
- **Oscillators** — OSC Phase Mod and Freq Mod acted on one sample per block; the SpectralFreeze oscillator played out of tune and went silent after a reset; the Formant oscillator went out of tune towards C8; the Additive oscillator's partials sat on whole FFT bins (now fractional, floor -70 dBc).
- **Controls that did nothing** — The Dice button, Mixer Spectral Shift, per-voice Morph Position in SpectralMorph mode, Formant Vowel (Morph is now an offset from the chosen vowel; old projects keep their sound), the free-run trance-gate Rate (stuck at 4 Hz), the Spectral Tilt destination, and the global LFO above about 20 Hz (it now reaches the 50 Hz the knob shows).
- **Filters** — The self-oscillating filter stopped ringing under cutoff modulation; a filter type switch jumped (it now crossfades); SVF drive stepped; the Comb filter at full resonance was 22 dB louder than the other types (its level is now compensated).
- **Delays** — Echoes came 6144 samples late through a hidden wet-path latency; the Spectral delay's Feedback did almost nothing after the first repeat and its output stepped at every analysis frame; changing its FFT Size could glitch; a Delay Time beyond what a type can hold is now visibly limited; the Spectral delay's stereo spread is the same on every render.
- **Harmonizer** — It collapsed the mix to mono and its limiter acted on the dry signal; it now keeps the stereo dry signal, limits the harmony only, and ramps its transitions.
- **Distortion** — Several types were silent or 24 dB quieter at Drive 0 (the low end of the drive range is now neutral; the rest of the law is unchanged); the Spectral distortion's Mix blended a dry signal that was out of time with the wet; the ChaosWaveshaper's Lorenz mode looped instead of staying chaotic.
- **Modulation** — Global route edits could leave the seven slot parameters out of step; voice-matrix destinations used two different numberings; a route whose source or destination changed briefly applied its old amount (a burst on preset switch); Master Volume and global filter modulation stepped; Arp Rate modulation fell off the tempo grid; voice-route Curve, Smooth and scales did not behave as shown.
- **Voices** — Note-off and steal bookkeeping could address the wrong note; Steal Mode and mono retrigger did not do what their names say; the mono voice was off centre; a SpectralMorph voice could replay the previous note.
- **Arpeggiator** — Retrigger Beat did nothing without host musical time; a single held key with a gate above 100 % played staccato; the first note after a pause could wait out the old step; step lengths were truncated by a sample and drifted against the tempo; keys took effect at the block start rather than their sample; skip highlights were sent from the audio thread; only two of the eight lanes showed a playhead; a pasted Modifier lane step stored the wrong value.
- **The output depended on the host buffer size** — The delays, the Hall reverb and the modulation grid rendered differently at different buffer sizes, so a bounce could differ from playback. Every section now renders the same at 32, 100, 441 and 2048 samples.
- **Preset loads caused dropouts at small buffers** — Loading a preset cleared every delay buffer in one block (2.5-3.3 ms of work); the clear is now spread over blocks (0.1 ms per block). Envelope curve tables are no longer rebuilt on every parameter update (252 to 17 µs with curved envelopes).
- **A browser preset load and a host restore could differ** — Loading from the preset browser skipped the voice routes and the engine and arp resets. Both now run the same code.
- **Host and editor** — Ruinae now reports its tail, silence and bus layout to hosts as the VST3 contract asks; editor-only switches no longer appear as automatable parameters; closing the editor could touch freed controls; 38 overlapping and 26 out-of-bounds controls in the editor are fixed; missing arp controls and hidden preset categories are back; the macOS AU reports the plugin's real version.
- **Release 0 clicked at note-off** — With the amp envelope's Release at 0, a note stopped within about 5 samples, which clicks. It now fades out over 2 ms, and the tail Ruinae reports to the host includes those 2 ms, so a host that stops processing at the end of the tail does not cut the fade. Factory presets are unaffected: their releases are all 50 ms or longer.
- **The Chaos, S&H and Random rate knobs showed and defaulted to the wrong rates** — The three knobs used the LFO's 0.01–50 Hz scale, while the sources run at 0.05–20x (Chaos) and 0.1–50 Hz (S&H, Random), so the displayed value and the default did not match what played. Each knob now uses its source's own range, and the defaults are the rates the processor starts at. Saved projects and presets keep their rates. Host automation recorded on these three knobs now maps to different rates, so re-check any automation lanes on them.
- **The modulation heatmap lit random cells and hid some routes** — The heatmap kept a grid smaller than the Global tab's 14 sources by 15 destinations, so its bottom rows showed cells that were not routed (a different pattern each time), and routes from Tran or ArpP, or to AGat, AOct, ASwg or ASpc, never appeared. Every source and destination now has its own cell.
- **The Digital delay's feedback above 100 % grew without limit** — Nothing inside the Digital delay's feedback loop held it back, so above 100 % the repeats grew louder inside the delay line on every pass and only the output limiter hid it. The loop now saturates above 100 %, so self-oscillation stays bounded. Below 100 % the Digital delay stays clean.
- **The Digital delay's limiter let one channel duck the other** — One limiter ran over the left channel and then the right, so a loud left channel turned the right channel down too. Each channel now has its own limiter.
- **The Tape delay's two channels ran through one shared transport** — The left and right channels shared one set of wow and flutter oscillators, oversampler and roll-off filter, so the wow and flutter ran twice as fast as set and the right channel started from the left channel's filter state. Both channels now share one tape transport and keep their own filters, so identical input gives identical output.
- **The Tape delay hissed with Wear and Age at 0** — With Wear and Age both at 0 the Tape delay still added hiss at about -88 dBFS with no input, so Ruinae never went silent while the Tape delay was on. At Wear 0 and Age 0 it is now silent; any Wear or Age above 0 hisses exactly as before.
- **The Tape delay mixed only part of a very large block** — In host blocks longer than 4096 samples, everything after the first 4096 samples stayed 100 % wet whatever the delay's Mix. Every sample is now mixed.
- **The mod matrix's curve menu named the wrong curves** — The menu listed Linear, Exponential, Logarithmic and S-Curve, but the third entry played an S-curve and the fourth a four-step staircase. The entries now read Linear, Exponential, S-Curve and Stepped; saved routes keep their sound and now show their real curve name.
- **The Stepped mod curve overshot its amount by a third** — With the source at full scale (a macro at 100 %, a square LFO), a Stepped route gave 4/3 of its amount. Its top step is now exactly the amount, so routes that hit full scale with this curve move less than before.
- **LFO 1, LFO 2 and Chaos Depth did nothing** — The Depth knobs shrank the drawn waveform, but every route from these sources still modulated at full depth. Depth now scales what the source sends to every route, and all three default to 100 %. Projects and presets saved before this version load at 100 %, the depth they always played at, so they sound the same.
- **Note velocity never changed the level** — Every note played at full level whatever its velocity, so the Velocity Curve, the arp Velocity lane, Accent and Humanize velocity were inaudible. A new **Velocity > Amp** knob (VEL, in the AMP envelope) sets how far velocity scales the level; it defaults to 100 %, and the factory presets now respond to velocity. Projects saved before this version load it at 0 %, the level they were made with.
- **The Spectral delay's repeats drifted off the tempo grid** — To make its first echo land on time, the Spectral delay's FFT latency was taken off its delay time, but its repeats are spaced by that shortened time, so every repeat came about 32 ms early at 1/4 note and 120 BPM (48 kHz), more with each repeat. The Spectral delay now runs at the set delay time: its repeats land on the tempo grid again (within one FFT hop), and its first echo arrives a fixed FFT size later than the other delay types (about 21 ms at 48 kHz with the default 1024-point FFT), like a short pre-delay. Spectral-delay presets with feedback get their repeats back on the beat.
- **A damaged preset or project loaded halfway** — When a preset file or project chunk ended early, inside its sound settings, Ruinae loaded the part it could read on top of the previous sound and reported success, so the patch became a mix of the two and the next save kept that mix. Such a file now fails to load and the current sound stays as it was; your host may report that the preset could not be loaded. Every complete preset and project loads as before.
- **A damaged preset or project could load out-of-range or NaN values** — Ruinae stored whatever a preset or project held, so a damaged file could load a menu index past the end of its menu or a NaN level, and the knobs showed values they cannot be set to. Every value now loads clamped to its knob's range, and a NaN or infinite value loads as that knob's default. Four factory presets stored a mod-matrix Smooth above the knob's 100 ms maximum (Frozen Spectral, Particle Storm, Dreamscape, Nebula Rise): loaded in a host they now smooth at 100 ms, as they already did from the preset browser. Twelve other factory presets were re-saved with values the sound engine already limited, so they sound the same.
- **A project saved by an older Ruinae picked up settings from the preset loaded before it** — Older versions of Ruinae saved fewer sections (sections such as the voice routes, the modulation sources, the harmonizer and the arpeggiator were added to the saved state over time), and loading such a project or preset kept whatever the previous sound had in the sections it did not contain. Those sections now load their defaults, in the sound and on the knobs alike. Projects and presets saved by this version contain every section and load as before.
- **Sixteen presets hit the output ceiling** — Lydian Aurora, Stab Machine, Chaos Garden, Reich Drift, Anvil Ring, Swarm Sub, Vocal Bass, Supersaw, Vox Machina, Cathedral Organ, Choir, Harmony Gate, Phase Pulse, Swing Vox, Vowel Sequencer and Vowel Cloud played at full scale or spent up to 9 % of the time above 0.85, so the limiter clipped them (Vox Machina's clipping also showed as a DC offset). Their Master Gain is lowered so each peaks below 0.99 and spends under 1 % of its samples above 0.85. They play quieter.
- **Chorus / Flanger / Phaser switches now sound the same at every buffer size** — After a modulation type switch, the new effect warms up for 25 ms before its 30 ms fade in, and the fade began at the start of the next buffer rather than the moment the warm-up ended, so the first quarter second after a switch differed slightly from one buffer size to another. The fade now starts at the exact sample the warm-up ends, whatever the buffer size.
- **The Comb filter clicked during fast cutoff sweeps at high resonance** — The Cutoff knob, its automation and global modulation reach the filter once per buffer, and the Comb filter jumped to each new pitch at once, by up to 11 samples of delay per step at the low end of the range. At high Resonance each jump clicked. A change of the Cutoff now glides the comb's pitch to its new value over 2 ms. A Cutoff that does not move sounds exactly as before, and the filter envelope, key tracking and voice routes still move the comb pitch sample by sample.
- **The Hall reverb's Size and Damping hardly changed its tail** — The Hall decayed in 0.4 to 2.2 seconds whatever its Size asked for (0.5 to 10 seconds), and Damping barely darkened the tail. Size now sets the Hall's decay time from 0.5 up to 10 seconds, and Damping darkens the tail, down to a twentieth of the decay time at the top of the spectrum at 100 %. Projects saved before this version and the factory presets that use the Hall load the Size and Damping that give their old tail, so they sound the same; the knobs show the new values.

Seraphis.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **The FX delay's Feedback did almost nothing after the first repeat** *(shared DSP)* — The spectral delay's feedback limiter worked on unscaled FFT values, so it squashed every recirculated frequency down to the same tiny level: the repeats after the first fell away by tens of dB and lost their tone colour. The limiter now works in the signal's own scale, so Feedback sustains the repeats as set and keeps their spectrum. Presets and projects with FX delay feedback above 0 repeat noticeably longer than before.
- **The FX delay stepped at every analysis frame** *(shared DSP)* — The spectral delay overlapped its frames without a synthesis window, so with feedback its output jumped at every frame edge. It now uses matched analysis and synthesis windows, and the steps are gone.
- **The FX delay's return fade moved in steps** — The 20 ms fade of the FX delay's return level was updated once per processing slice, so it moved as a staircase with a small jump at each slice. It now moves sample by sample.

Vorago.notes_markdown:
### Fixed

- **Notes held by the latch or the sustain pedal kept sounding after a browser preset load** — Loading a preset from the preset browser only changed the controls; the sound engine's own load code never ran, so latched and sustained notes from the previous preset carried on into the new one. A browser load now runs the same code as a project reload: it releases those notes and resets sustain and channel pressure. Older presets and projects are also converted by one shared routine on both paths, so they load the same way from the browser and from the host.
